W1.name: Ines Okafor
W1.text: Ines Okafor was the only passenger on the ferry to Harrow Quay.
W1.quote: Ines Okafor was its only passenger.

W2.name: Tobiah Wren
W2.text: Tobiah Wren was the ferryman who transported Ines Okafor to the island.
W2.quote: The ferryman was an old man named Tobiah Wren.

W3.name: Aldous Brandt
W3.text: Aldous Brandt was the previous keeper of the Salt Ledger.

G1.text: Ines Okafor was tasked with becoming the new keeper of the Salt Ledger.

E1.text: Tobiah Wren informed Ines Okafor that Aldous Brandt had been gone for three weeks.

E2.text: Tobiah Wren gave Ines Okafor a small brass key that Aldous Brandt had given him.
E2.quote: It was a small brass key, no longer than her finger,

E3.text: Tobiah Wren warned Ines Okafor to keep the brass key off the ledger and away from the council.
E3.quote: Do not show it to the council.

Q1.text: The text does not state what the small brass key opens.
Q1.quote: He did not say, and I did not ask.

W4.name: Mara Venn
W4.text: Mara Venn was the Harbourmaster who met Ines Okafor.

G2.text: Ines Okafor needed to finish the audit of the Salt Ledger before the equinox market.
G2.quote: The council needs the audit finished before the equinox market,

E4.text: Mara Venn led Ines Okafor to the archive where the Salt Ledger was located.
E4.quote: She led Ines up the tower stairs to the archive,

E5.text: Ines Okafor discovered that the spring pages were torn out of the Salt Ledger.
E5.quote: The spring pages are missing," she said.

E6.text: Mara Venn stated that she knew nothing about the missing pages.
E6.quote: I say only what I know, and I know nothing."

Q2.text: What does Anselm Pike know about the Salt Ledger that he offers to Ines Okafor?
Q2.quote: I have known every account on this island

G3.text: Ines Okafor was trying to find anyone who had worked with Aldous Brandt.
G3.quote: Ines went looking for anyone who had worked with Brandt

E7.text: Ines Okafor spoke with Mara Lisle, who worked in the net loft.
E7.quote: A girl of about nineteen sat there among heaps

E8.text: Mara Lisle stated that Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping in his last month.
E8.quote: He went down to the salt warehouse at night

E9.text: Mara Lisle mentioned that Aldous Brandt was counting barrels at night.

Q3.text: What does the small black seabird in ink signify on the folded paper?
Q3.quote: In place of a signature someone had drawn a small black seabird

W5.name: Ines Okafor
W5.text: Ines Okafor was the one who counted the salt.

W6.name: Mara Venn
W6.text: Mara Venn was the harbourmaster who denied Ines Okafor access to the warehouse.
W6.quote: Not without an order from the council,

G4.text: Ines Okafor was trying to count the salt to verify the ledger's records.

E10.text: Ines Okafor discovered a printed handbill pasted over the November page of the ledger.
E10.quote: A printed handbill had been pasted over the margin

E11.text: Ines Okafor dismissed the printed handbill as a prank from the dock boys.
E11.quote: It made no sense to her, and she took it

E12.text: Ines Okafor asked Mara Venn to open the salt warehouse for counting the barrels.
E12.quote: she asked the harbourmaster to open the salt warehouse

Q4.text: The text does not state what the second note under the door signifies.
Q4.quote: That night there was a second note under the door

W7.name: Dr Pike
W7.text: Dr Pike owned the dispensary that housed the island's only press.
W7.quote: the press stood in the back room of Dr Pike's dispensary.

G5.text: Ines Okafor was trying to carry her salt count tally to the council the next morning.
G5.quote: She meant to carry this tally to the council in the morning.

E13.text: Ines Okafor copied her salt count onto a single sheet, noting forty barrels in the book and sixty-four on the receipts.
E13.quote: She copied her salt count onto a single sheet: forty barrels in the book, sixty-four on the receipts, month by month.

E14.text: Ines Okafor heard the street door open and someone climbing the stairs late at night.
E14.quote: A little before midnight she heard the street door open at the foot of the tower.

E15.text: The archive lamp went out while Ines Okafor was in the room.

Q5.text: The text does not state who entered the archive or why they took the tally.
Q5.quote: She did not know who had stood beside her in the dark

W8.name: Dr Pike
W8.text: Dr Pike owned the dispensary that housed the island's only press.
W8.quote: Dr Pike found her on the tower steps and was all concern.

E16.text: Dr Pike found Ines Okafor on the tower steps and listened to her story.
E16.quote: Dr Pike found her on the tower steps and was all concern.

E17.text: Dr Pike offered Ines Okafor his strongbox in the dispensary for safekeeping.
E17.quote: I have a strongbox in the dispensary, and nobody searches a doctor.

Q6.text: What does the discrepancy between the printed tide table and the actual water level suggest about the harbour?
Q6.quote: But she had run to this window at midnight, and the water had been high

W9.name: Mara Lisle
W9.text: Mara Lisle is a net-mender who spoke with Ines Okafor.
W9.quote: Mara Lisle listened to everything, and when Ines had finished

W10.name: The Cormorant
W10.text: The Cormorant is a figure who wrote to the keeper.

G6.text: Ines Okafor was trying to find the missing spring pages of the Salt Ledger.

E18.text: Mara Lisle showed Ines Okafor a bottle of black ink and a pen.
E18.quote: Mara Lisle listened to everything, and when Ines had finished

E19.text: The Cormorant revealed seeing boats arrive at night when the tide table predicted dry steps.
E19.quote: I saw the boats come in at night, twice, at an hour

E20.text: The Cormorant stated that Dr Pike's men rolled barrels up from the outer steps.
E20.quote: Dr Pike's men rolled barrels up from the outer steps.

Q7.text: What was the significance of the brass case that was not a door?
Q7.quote: she thought of the one brass case she had never tried

W11.name: Dr Pike
W11.text: Dr Pike was the person whose men came for Aldous Brandt.
W11.quote: When Pike's men came for him

W12.name: The Crane Company
W12.text: The Crane Company was an entity whose offer was refused by the council.
W12.quote: The Crane Company's offer was refused

G7.text: Ines Okafor was trying to secure the spring pages of the Salt Ledger.
G7.quote: Ines laid the spring pages on the council table.

G8.text: Ines Okafor was trying to record the true salt count in the Salt Ledger.
G8.quote: entered the true count beneath them: sixty-four barrels

E21.text: Tobiah Wren brought Aldous Brandt back to the island on the morning of the market.
E21.quote: Tobiah Wren came up the harbour steps on the morning of the market

E22.text: Tobiah Wren had hidden Aldous Brandt for three weeks in the light-keeper's hut.
E22.quote: Tobiah had hidden him for three weeks in the light-keeper's hut

E23.text: Mara Venn admitted to taking the tally that Ines Okafor had made.

Q8.text: What does the hand of Aldous Brandt signify when he says it is good?
Q8.quote: Aldous Brandt watched from the windowsill and said the hand was good.

dropped.quote: Anselm Pike. I am the physician here
dropped.text: Anselm Pike was the physician and printer on the island.

dropped.quote: Mara Lisle. The harbourmaster is Mara Venn.
dropped.text: Mara Lisle was a girl of about nineteen who worked in the net loft and ran Brandt's errands.

dropped.quote: Give me the receipts, Ines. The tin, tonight
dropped.text: Ines Okafor was trying to secure a safe place to keep her salt count receipts.

dropped.quote: Give me the receipts, Ines. The tin, tonight
dropped.text: Dr Pike suggested Ines Okafor give him the receipts to keep them safe.

units.title: 7. The Door That Isn't a Door

dropped.text: Aldous Brandt was the old keeper who had not left the island of his own will.
